title: An Ubuntu-Guided Large Language Model Framework for Cognitive Behavioral Mental Health Dialogue
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the model's ability to appropriately integrate Christian faith-based support (e.g., scripture, prayer) into a therapeutic chatbot conversation to provide culturally and spiritually resonant comfort for mental health issues within a South African context.
findings: The study found that integrating faith-based elements, specifically Christian scripture, was a feasible and important part of creating a culturally adapted mental health chatbot for the South African context. The fine-tuned model successfully used spiritual language and scriptural references to provide comfort and grounding, aligning with the Ubuntu philosophy's emphasis on spirituality. However, expert psychological evaluators, trained in predominantly secular Western frameworks, gave lower ratings to the faith-based integrations, highlighting a cultural gap in professional practice and reinforcing the study's rationale for adapting interventions to include spiritual realities relevant to the target population.
